{{Recipe}}

'''Nigerian eggplant fufu''' is a [[Cookbook:Swallow|swallow]] made from eggplants Despite the dark purple colour of eggplant, it turns a dark greyish colour as in [[Cookbook:Amala Ọgẹdẹ (Nigerian Plantain Fufu)|amala]] when cooked.

== Ingredients ==
*2 [[Cookbook:Eggplant|eggplants]]

*2 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoons]] [[Cookbook:Psyllium|psyllium]] husk powder

== Equipment ==
*[[Cookbook:Pots and Pans|Pot]]
*[[Cookbook:Food Processor|Food processor]]
*[[Cookbook:Paper Towel|Paper towels]]

== Procedure ==
#Cut the eggplant into small pieces and soften in a pot of boiling water. Drain well.
#Absorb excess water from the eggplant with paper towels, then [[Cookbook:Puréeing|blend]] with the food processor.
#Transfer the eggplant purée to a pot, and stir over medium heat for 2 minutes.
#Add the psyllium husk, and stir for additional 3 minutes.
#Shape into desired portions.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==
*Choose small or medium-sized eggplant for your fufu, as they contain fewer seeds and are sweeter. It is also best to use eggplant with indentations since they are sweeter and have fewer seeds.
